body: ExitPlanMode is out of scope for TASK-038: plan approval has its own choices (approve with auto-accept or manual edits, keep planning with feedback) whose mapping to a hook allow/deny and the resulting permission mode is undocumented, the plan often exceeds 4096 chars, and plan approval may already reach Telegram as a channel permission_request (probe item e). Alternative rejected: reuse the question path for ExitPlanMode in this task.

Questions go to a new hub path /v1/question (QuestionPost with the questions, answers returned by index as QuestionAnswer); the hook keeps the original tool_input and builds updatedInput itself, so capped texts never become answer keys. Alternative rejected: extend /v1/permission and PermissionPost with a question variant (mixes two answer shapes in one endpoint and one oneshot type).

The question hook is `cctg hook PreToolUse` registered with matcher AskUserQuestion and dispatched inside hook::run by tool_name (as the task and its acceptance test name it). Alternative rejected: a separate command-line event name like ToolStatus (`cctg hook AskUserQuestion`).

Hub-side wait for a question is 300 s (hook 310 s, settings timeout 330 s) with a Telegram button that lets the hook go at once; the long wait favours the remote user because after the timeout the question is only answerable in the terminal. Alternative rejected: a short 60-90 s wait like the permission hook. Final value is an open question for the user.

Probe (d) showed Esc kills the waiting question hook and rejects the call without a dialog; per PLAN section 6 this is documented in docs/poc.md (and the verified facts in CLAUDE.md Hooks) while the statusMessage text stays as in the reference. Alternative rejected: add an Esc hint to statusMessage in docs/hook-settings.json, install.sh and poc.md (three copies plus the hook_cli shape test for a text Claude Code shows only as a spinner).

git apply --ignore-whitespace --3way of task038.patch (checked out with CRLF under core.autocrlf) wrote CRLF lines into the index and mixed endings into the working files; install_e2e::the_script_has_unix_line_endings failed on install.sh lines 542-545. Fixed by rewriting every patched file with LF and restaging (git ls-files --eol shows i/lf); LF-byte hashes unchanged. Next time apply with a CR-stripped copy of the patch.

Rated the loss of the Telegram signal for AskUserQuestion on installs updated by the button (old settings.json, hub now drops the PermissionRequest of the question) as minor and kept the verdict SHIP, because PLAN section 7 accepts that the hook needs an install.sh rerun and the acceptance criteria hold. Alternative rejected: NEEDS_WORK until the hub sends a fallback notice for questions without a PreToolUse hook.

The PermissionRequest hook of AskUserQuestion now posts to the hub again (build_permission Skip removed); the hub still answers no decision at once and, unless a question hook of that session asked within 340 s, sends one plain notice per session that the client lacks the PreToolUse hook. Alternative rejected: keep the Skip in the hook, which would make the notice unreachable for exactly the clients it is for (new binary via the update button, old settings).

The hub answers questions with option indexes plus the typed text (wire::Answered) and the hook builds the answer from the labels of the original tool_input; the first-build label-string answer is now BadResponse (feature unreleased). Alternative rejected: stop capping/trimming labels in the post and keep sending label strings, which still ties the answer to what the hub displayed.

With the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR another worktree's build replaced the cctg lib test binary (same metadata hash for both worktrees): cargo test -- --list showed no hub::questions tests and ran stale code while reporting Finished. Touching crates/cctg/src/lib.rs before each test run forced a rebuild from this worktree; the final workspace run was done that way.
